sub: From a distance that is just right to an earth entrusted to us, eight units reveal the home God prepared for humanity.

questions.q: Why is the earth just right for life?
What does my next breath, or a glass of water, have to do with God?

units.title: A Distance That's Just Right
units.sub: A little closer and we'd be Venus; a little farther and we'd be Mars. Earth sits in exactly the right place.

share.v: who established it and didn’t create it a waste, who formed it to be inhabited

blocks.h: The surface of Venus is hotter than 460°C, hot enough to melt lead. On Mars the air pressure is less than one percent of Earth's, so liquid water can hardly survive on the surface. Tucked between the two, Earth averages about 15°C, and rivers, lakes and seas flow everywhere.
For Yahweh who created the heavens, the God who formed the earth and made it, who established it and didn’t create it a waste, who formed it to be inhabited says: “I am Yahweh. There is no other.
The habitable zone

Astronomers call the range of distances around a star where a planet's surface could hold liquid water the “habitable zone.” For our Sun, this range is estimated to begin at about 0.95 astronomical units, with the outer edge estimated at somewhere between 1.4 and 1.7 astronomical units, depending on the model. Earth sits at 1 astronomical unit, about 150 million kilometers from the Sun.
It's like warming yourself around a campfire: too close and you get scorched, too far and you freeze. Earth sits in the spot that is just warm enough, and it stays there all year round.
A nearly circular orbit

Earth's orbit around the Sun is very nearly a perfect circle, with an eccentricity of only about 0.017. If the orbit were stretched out flat like those of many exoplanets, each year would swing wildly between scorching heat and bitter cold.

The Sun itself is also remarkably steady. It is a stable, middle-aged star, and over one solar cycle its brightness varies by only about one part in a thousand, unlike many stars that erupt in violent flares.
Distance isn't the only requirement. Earth also needs the right amount of atmosphere and greenhouse effect: with no greenhouse gases at all, the average surface temperature would drop to about −18°C.

The boundaries of the habitable zone are still being studied, and they depend on atmospheric composition, cloud cover and planetary mass. Astronomers have discovered thousands of exoplanets, but none has yet been confirmed to have all of these Earth-like conditions at once.
The surface temperature of Venus is above about 460°C; the surface air pressure on Mars is less than one percent of Earth's.
Earth's orbital eccentricity is about 0.017, close to a perfect circle.
The Sun's habitable zone begins at about 0.95 astronomical units, with the outer edge estimated at 1.4 to 1.7 astronomical units, depending on the model.
That Earth meets so many conditions for habitability at once points to a God who made the earth “to be inhabited.” This is an inference of faith.
His goodness: a home prepared for us
Isaiah says God “didn’t create it a waste,” but “formed it to be inhabited.” Earth isn't a landing spot we stumbled onto by chance. It is a home a loving Father prepared for His children.
The heavens are the heavens of Yahweh; but he has given the earth to the children of men.
He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.
In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you.
The God who prepared the earth for us has also prepared an eternal home for us in Jesus Christ.
Look out the window: there is air, there is water, there is just the right temperature. All the things we have every day and never think about are God's grace.
Reflect: What are three things you take for granted today that are actually gifts from God?
Prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for preparing this home for me. Help me stop taking Your grace for granted, and to offer You thanks every day. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Give thanks in everything: count your blessings one by one, and the glory goes to God.
Return to our proper place: it isn't that we adapted to the earth; God prepared the earth for us.
Build your relationship with God first: knowing the One who prepared it all matters more than enjoying what He prepared.

blocks.h: This week: every night before bed, write down three things you're thankful for, for seven days in a row.
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the “habitable zone”?
o: The range of distances where a planet's surface could hold liquid water
The best area to build a house
quiz.e: For our Sun, it begins at about 0.95 astronomical units.

quiz.q: What is special about Earth's orbit?
o: It is very nearly a perfect circle
It is very long and flat
quiz.e: Its eccentricity is only about 0.017.

quiz.q: According to Isaiah 45:18, why did God create the earth?
quiz.e: “He didn’t create it a waste, He formed it to be inhabited.”

units.title: The Gift of the Moon
units.sub: The moon doesn't just light up the night sky. It steadies Earth's tilt and drives the ocean tides.

share.v: He appointed the moon for seasons. The sun knows when to set.

blocks.h: Compared with its planet, our moon is unusually large: its diameter is about a quarter of Earth's. This big moon is like a hand steadying a spinning top, keeping Earth's axis from wobbling wildly.
God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.
Stable seasons

Earth's axis is tilted about 23.4 degrees, which gives us spring, summer, autumn and winter. Over long periods, this angle only drifts slowly between about 22 and 24.5 degrees. Calculations by French astronomer Jacques Laskar show that the moon's gravity is a major reason Earth's axis stays stable.
Mars, which has no large moon, has seen its axial tilt swing dramatically over long periods, possibly anywhere from near 0 degrees to more than 60 degrees, with its climate lurching along with it.
Picture a spinning top with someone gently holding it steady. It spins smoothly. The moon is that steadying hand on the earth.
The heartbeat of the ocean

The moon's gravity causes the tides, with about twice the tidal effect of the Sun. Every day, high and low tides stir the seawater, making the coastal intertidal zone one of the richest places for life.
Some research suggests that even without the moon, the changes in Earth's axis might be milder than early estimates. Just how much the moon contributes to axial stability is still being discussed.
Earth's axial tilt is about 23.4 degrees and varies over long periods between about 22 and 24.5 degrees.
The moon contributes significantly to the long-term stability of Earth's tilt; studies differ on how much it would vary without the moon.
The axial tilt of Mars shows large, chaotic variations over long periods.
The moon's tidal effect is about twice that of the Sun.
He appointed the moon for seasons. The sun knows when to set.
His faithfulness: steady seasons
Farmers can sow and harvest on time because the seasons are stable. Behind those stable seasons is a moon placed just right, and the One who placed the moon is the faithful God.
It will be established forever like the moon, the faithful witness in the sky.” Selah.
Psalm 89 uses the moon as a witness to God's covenant with David. The moon rises day after day like a witness in the sky, reminding us that God's promises never change.
Look at the moon tonight. It gives off no light of its own, yet it reflects the light of the Sun and lights up the dark.
Reflect: Am I like the moon, reflecting the light of Christ, or am I trying to shine on my own?
Prayer: Lord, You are the One who holds my life steady. When my life wobbles, hold me up, so that I can stand firm in You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Selflessness: the moon doesn't give off its own light; it only reflects the Sun. It is no longer I, but Christ who lives in me.
Let Jesus receive the glory: when people see something good in me, let them see that Jesus is the source of the light.
Become a spiritual companion: just as the moon steadies the earth, I can be a steady presence in someone else's life.

blocks.h: This week: reach out to a friend whose life has been unsettled lately, and spend some time with them.
Quiz

quiz.q: How does the moon help Earth's seasons?
o: It helps stabilize the tilt of Earth's axis
quiz.e: The moon's gravity is a major reason Earth's axis stays stable over the long term.

quiz.q: About how strong are the moon's tides compared with the Sun's?
quiz.e: The moon is much closer than the Sun, so its tidal effect is about twice as strong.

quiz.q: Does the moon produce its own light?
o: No, it reflects the Sun's light
Yes, it burns on its own
quiz.e: The moon reflects the Sun's light, just as we reflect the light of Christ.

units.title: Wonderful Water
units.sub: The most ordinary substance, with the most extraordinary properties.

share.v: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.

blocks.h: When almost any substance turns from liquid to solid, it shrinks, gets denser and sinks. Water does the opposite: ice is lighter than water and floats on top.

If ice sank, lakes and oceans would freeze from the bottom up, layer by layer, and many water creatures could not survive the winter. Because ice floats, it acts like a blanket over the water below, protecting the life within.
In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
A few unusual things about water

items: Ice is lighter than water: ice has a density of about 0.917 grams per cubic centimeter, about nine percent less than liquid water; water is densest at 4°C.
Very high specific heat: water can absorb or release a great deal of heat while its temperature changes only a little. This makes the oceans Earth's thermostat and keeps our body temperature steady.
Evaporation absorbs a lot of heat: that's why sweating cools us so well.
It dissolves many substances: nutrients, salts and oxygen all rely on water to carry them through our bodies and the soil.
Surface tension and capillary action: these help water climb from a tree's roots to treetops 100 meters high.

blocks.h: Water molecules are like people holding hands (hydrogen bonds), holding on not too tightly and not too loosely. It's this just-right “hand-holding” that gives water so many wonderful properties.

In 1913, Harvard physiological chemist Lawrence Henderson published The Fitness of the Environment, carefully listing the many ways water is “fit” for life, and arguing that the environment itself seems to have been prepared for life.
More recent research has found that water isn't just a passive background inside cells. It actively takes part in life processes such as protein folding and molecular recognition.
Ice is less dense than liquid water, and water is densest at about 4°C.
Water's specific heat and heat of vaporization are exceptionally high among common liquids.
Water actively takes part in biochemical processes in cells; the detailed mechanisms are still being studied.
That so many of water's properties benefit life at once points to purposeful design. This is a philosophical argument that goes back to Henderson.
His wisdom: wonder hidden in the ordinary
God often hides His deepest wisdom in the most ordinary things. We drink a glass of water every day, yet few people know how wonderful it is.
As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.
Our bodies can't live without water, and our souls can't live without God. At a well, Jesus said to a Samaritan woman:
but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.
He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, from within him will flow rivers of living water.
Pour a glass of water and drink it slowly. Thank God for this wonderful gift.
Reflect: Has my soul been dry lately, or refreshed by living water?
Prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the spring of living water. Satisfy the thirst in my heart, and let living water flow out from me to refresh others. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Holy Spirit is my guide: the rivers of living water refer to the Holy Spirit (John 7:39). Ask to be filled with the Spirit every day.
Receive with your heart, relying on the Spirit: don't just understand with your head; receive with your heart.
Multiplication: living water is meant to flow out. Share what you received today with one person.

blocks.h: This week: every time you drink water, pray a short prayer of thanks.
Quiz

quiz.q: How does floating ice help the creatures in a lake?
o: It covers the water below like a blanket so they can survive the winter
It makes the lake freeze faster
quiz.e: Lakes freeze from the top, and the water below stays liquid.

quiz.q: What is the benefit of water's high specific heat?
o: It keeps the oceans and our body temperature stable
quiz.e: Water absorbs and releases large amounts of heat with little change in temperature.

quiz.q: What did Jesus mean by “rivers of living water”?
quiz.e: “But he said this about the Spirit, which those believing in him were to receive.” (John 7:39)

units.title: The Invisible Shield
units.sub: The magnetic field, the atmosphere and the ozone layer protect life on earth day and night.

share.v: He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart.

blocks.h: The Sun constantly blasts out charged particles, called the “solar wind,” at hundreds of kilometers per second. Around Earth is an invisible magnetic field that keeps most of the solar wind out.

The northern and southern lights are what happens when a few particles slip in along magnetic field lines into the high atmosphere over the poles and glow as they strike the air. The beautiful curtain of light you see is actually the shield at work.
He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
Three layers of protection

items: Magnetic field: generated by flowing liquid iron in Earth's outer core, it blocks most of the solar wind and cosmic rays.
Atmosphere: about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen; most meteors burn up in it before reaching the ground.
Ozone layer: located in the stratosphere, it absorbs most harmful ultraviolet B and almost all ultraviolet C.

blocks.h: Mars lost its global magnetic field long ago. NASA's MAVEN mission found that much of Mars' atmosphere has been stripped away into space by the solar wind.
Earth is like a spaceship surrounded by intense radiation and particle storms. The magnetic field is the hull, the atmosphere is the airtight cabin, and the ozone layer is the UV-blocking glass.
The ozone layer on the mend

In the late twentieth century, man-made chlorofluorocarbons damaged the ozone layer, and an “ozone hole” appeared over Antarctica. In 1987 nations signed the Montreal Protocol to phase out these substances. The World Meteorological Organization's 2022 assessment found that the ozone layer is gradually recovering, and over Antarctica it is expected to return to 1980 levels around 2066.
Earth's magnetic field is generated by flowing liquid metal in the outer core and deflects most of the solar wind.
The ozone layer absorbs most ultraviolet B and almost all ultraviolet C.
After losing its global magnetic field, Mars had much of its atmosphere stripped away by the solar wind; how much was lost, and over what time, is still being studied.
Since the Montreal Protocol, the ozone layer has been gradually recovering.
He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart.
His goodness: protection that never stops
The magnetic field never rests, and the ozone layer never takes a day off. God's protection is like that: even while we sleep, He keeps watch over us.
Yahweh is your keeper. Yahweh is your shade on your right hand. The sun will not harm you by day, nor the moon by night.
It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in,
Think back over the past year. What dangers did you only find out about afterward? God's protection is often invisible.
Reflect: What have I been afraid of lately? Place it “in the shadow of the Almighty.”
Prayer: Lord, my protector, thank You for surrounding me with an invisible shield. I will no longer try to fend off everything on my own; I take refuge under Your wings. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus reign: I don't have to be my own shield. Let the Lord take charge and protect me.
The responsibility of a steward: humanity once damaged the ozone layer, and humanity worked together to repair it. God has entrusted us to keep watch over this earth.
Comrades in arms: stand watch in prayer for your family and your brothers and sisters, and become a protection for one another.

blocks.h: This week: pray every day for the safety of three family members or friends, and tell one of them that you are praying for them.
Quiz

quiz.q: What does Earth's magnetic field mainly block?
o: Charged particles from the solar wind
quiz.e: The magnetic field deflects most of the solar wind and cosmic rays.

quiz.q: What does the ozone layer mainly absorb?
quiz.e: It absorbs most ultraviolet B and almost all ultraviolet C.

quiz.q: What causes the northern and southern lights?
o: Charged particles striking the upper atmosphere and glowing
quiz.e: Particles enter the polar regions along magnetic field lines and glow as they strike the atmosphere.

units.title: The Breathing Earth
units.sub: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen; we take in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide.

share.v: he himself gives to all life and breath, and all things.

blocks.h: Some of the oxygen molecules in the breath you just took may have come from invisible phytoplankton in the ocean. About half of all photosynthesis on Earth takes place in the sea.
in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?
A global exchange

Plants, algae and some bacteria use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugars, releasing oxygen. Animals and people breathe in oxygen, break down sugars for energy, and breathe out carbon dioxide. Back and forth, the two form the carbon and oxygen cycle.
It's like two neighbors trading things over the fence every day: you give me what I need, I give you what you need, and nobody owes anybody.
The most abundant protein on earth
The enzyme that “grabs” carbon dioxide is called Rubisco, and it may well be the most abundant protein on Earth.
Carbon dioxide makes up only about four parts in ten thousand of the atmosphere, yet that is enough to supply every plant on earth, and it also helps maintain the surface temperature.

Photosynthesis is a precise chain of steps: capturing photons, splitting water molecules, passing electrons along and building energy molecules. Its efficiency and regulation are still a hot topic of research.
About half of global primary production (photosynthesis) takes place in the ocean.
Rubisco is one of the most abundant proteins on Earth; estimates of its total global amount remain uncertain.
Carbon dioxide makes up about four parts in ten thousand of the atmosphere (about 420 ppm).
Plants and animals supply each other's needs, forming a mutually supporting system that points to a wise Designer.
He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath, and all things.
His goodness: every breath is grace
We breathe more than 20,000 times a day, yet we hardly ever think about it. Every breath is given freely by God through a wonderful cycle.
Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit!
At creation, God breathed into man and he became a living being. The risen Jesus breathed on His disciples, and they received the Holy Spirit and became new creations.
Quietly take five deep breaths. Each time you breathe in, say “Lord,” and each time you breathe out, say “thank You.”
Reflect: If every breath is a gift from God, what words will I speak with this breath?
Prayer: God who gives the breath of life, thank You for every breath. May my mouth open to praise You, and may I use the breath You give to bless others. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Deny yourself: plants give their oxygen away to others. Live for Jesus and for others, not for yourself.
The order of relationships: first a living exchange with God, then a living exchange with people.
Let everything that has breath praise Yah (Psalm 150:6).

blocks.h: This week: put a plant at home or on your desk, and every time you see it, pray for someone.
Quiz

quiz.q: About how much of Earth's photosynthesis takes place in the ocean?
quiz.e: Phytoplankton in the ocean contribute about half of primary production.

quiz.q: Photosynthesis turns which two things into sugars?
quiz.e: And it releases oxygen.

quiz.q: What did the risen Jesus say when He breathed on His disciples?
quiz.e: John 20:22.

units.title: The Journey of Water
units.sub: From ocean to cloud, from rain to river, a single drop of water travels the whole world.

share.v: For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and doesn’t return there, but waters the earth, and makes it grow and bud,

blocks.h: Every year the Sun evaporates about 500,000 cubic kilometers of water from the oceans and land. It rises into the sky and falls again as rain and snow. A water molecule stays in the atmosphere for only about nine days on average before returning to the ground.
All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.
A cycle that never stops

items: Evaporation: sunlight warms the sea surface, and water rises as vapor, leaving the salt behind in the sea.
Condensation: the vapor cools high in the sky and condenses into clouds.
Precipitation: water droplets in the clouds grow larger and fall as rain or snow.
Runoff and infiltration: water flows into rivers, soaks into the ground, and eventually returns to the sea.

blocks.h: The Sun is like a giant water-purification plant, distilling salty seawater into fresh water every day and delivering it free of charge to the mountains, the fields and your kitchen tap.
Precious fresh water

About 97% of Earth's water is in the oceans. Fresh water makes up only about 2.5%, and most of that is frozen in glaciers and ice caps. The fresh water in rivers and lakes that we can use directly is a tiny fraction of the total, yet the water cycle keeps renewing it without end.

Some three thousand years ago, the book of Job already described it: “For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor, which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.” (Job 36:27–28)
Global evaporation totals about 500,000 cubic kilometers per year.
The average residence time of a water molecule in the atmosphere is about eight to ten days.
About 97% of Earth's water is seawater; fresh water is about 2.5%, and most of it is ice.
A self-renewing water-purification system displays the faithfulness and provision of the Creator.

For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and doesn’t return there, but waters the earth, and makes it grow and bud, and gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater; so is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
His faithfulness: His word never fails
When rain falls, it always produces results. God uses the water cycle as a picture: His word is the same. Once spoken, it will surely be fulfilled.
For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor, which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.
The next time it rains, don't just think of the inconvenience. Remember that God is watering the earth once again.
Reflect: What word has God spoken to me that I am still waiting to see fulfilled?
Prayer: Faithful God, Your word never returns to You void. I believe that what You have spoken over my life will be fulfilled. Water my dry heart like the rain. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: God's word is like rain; receive it every day, and your life will bud and bear fruit.
The eight steps of changing our mindset: information, revelation, conviction, practice, review, correction, repetition, multiplication. Let the word keep cycling through your life.
Multiplication: what I have received must flow out to water others.

blocks.h: This week: memorize Isaiah 55:11 and write it out for a friend who is waiting on God.
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the main source of energy that drives the water cycle?
quiz.e: Sunlight warms the sea surface, causing water to evaporate and rise.

quiz.q: About how much of Earth's water is fresh water?
quiz.e: About 97% is seawater; fresh water is only about 2.5%.

quiz.q: In Isaiah 55, what do the rain and snow picture?
o: God's word, which will not return void
quiz.e: “So is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void.”

units.title: The Living Ground
units.sub: From the tectonic plates deep below to the soil beneath our feet, the earth is always moving and always nurturing life.

share.v: What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word, and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit, and brings forth, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.

blocks.h: A small pinch of healthy soil is home to hundreds of millions of microbes, more than the number of people on earth. Quietly they break down fallen leaves and return nutrients to the plants.
As for the earth, out of it comes bread. Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire. Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.
A crust that moves

Earth's outer shell is divided into many plates that move slowly. Earth is the only planet known to have active plate tectonics. Plate movement builds mountains and forms mineral deposits, and it carries carbonates from the seafloor back into Earth's interior, where volcanoes later release carbon dioxide.
This “carbonate–silicate cycle” works like a long-term thermostat: when Earth warms, rock weathering speeds up and absorbs more carbon dioxide; when it cools, weathering slows down.
It's like the thermostat on an air conditioner: when it's too hot, it cools harder; when it's too cold, it eases off, keeping the room comfortable.
Life beneath our feet

Soil isn't just dirt and sand. It is a living system made of rock fragments, organic matter, water, air and countless living things. A single gram of soil may hold thousands of different kinds of microbes.
The vast majority of soil microbial diversity has not yet been named or studied, and it has been called one of biology's “final frontiers.”
Earth is the only planet currently known to have active plate tectonics.
The carbonate–silicate cycle helps stabilize Earth's long-term temperature; its strength and time scale are still being studied.
Soil contains extremely rich microbial communities, most of which have not yet been studied.
The earth's regulating and life-nurturing functions display a God who makes the land bring forth its produce and provides for every living thing.
You visit the earth, and water it. You greatly enrich it.
His wisdom: the unseen workers
No one sees the microbes in the soil, yet they feed the whole earth. God, too, often uses unseen people and unseen things to accomplish great things.
When Jesus told the parable of the sower, the focus wasn't the seed, but the soil:
What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word, and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit, and brings forth, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.
If you can, go outside and touch the soil. That is a place where God is at work every day.
Reflect: Is my heart like the roadside, the rocky ground, the thorns, or the good soil?
Prayer: Lord, break up the hard ground of my heart. Remove the stones and thorns, and make me good soil, so that Your word may bear a hundredfold fruit in me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Humility: “humility” and “humus” (soil) share the same root. A humble heart is good soil.
Life first, then relationships, then ministry: fruit grows out of good soil. When our life is healthy, ministry naturally bears fruit.
Serve quietly: like the microbes in the soil, don't seek to be seen; seek only to nourish others.

blocks.h: This week: do one act of service that nobody knows about, seen only by your Father in heaven (Matthew 6:4).
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the only planet currently known to have active plate tectonics?
quiz.e: Plate tectonics helps regulate Earth's long-term temperature.

quiz.q: In the parable of the sower, which soil produces a hundredfold?
quiz.e: “What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word, and understands it.”

quiz.q: What work do the microbes in the soil do?
o: Break down organic matter and return nutrients to plants
quiz.e: They are the earth's unseen workers.

units.title: The Earth Is Yahweh's
units.sub: The earth is full of God's riches. God has entrusted it to us, to cultivate it and keep it.

share.v: The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it.

blocks.h: Scientists estimate that there may be about 8.7 million species of eukaryotic life on Earth, yet only about 1.2 million have been formally named so far. In other words, most of the creatures God made, we have yet to meet.
Yahweh, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches.
An interconnected web

Bees pollinate flowers, and flowers feed the bees; forests hold the soil and water in place, and rivers nourish the forests. Every living thing in an ecosystem is connected to others. Lose one link, and the whole web is affected.
It's like a tightly woven net: cut one thread and it seems like nothing, but cut too many and the whole net falls apart.
Our place in it all

Human beings are the only creatures able to study, understand and consciously care for the whole earth. We can destroy, and we can also restore. The worldwide effort to repair the ozone layer is one example.
The Bible gives humanity the role not of owner, but of steward: the earth belongs to God, we are entrusted to manage it, and one day we will give an account to Him.
There are about 8.7 million species of eukaryotes on Earth (an estimate), of which about 1.2 million have been named.
Species in an ecosystem depend on one another, for example through pollination and food webs.
Humans are entrusted stewards, not owners. This is the biblical worldview.
The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it.
His righteousness and goodness: entrusting and caring
Yahweh God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
God placing the world into human hands is an act of trust in us, and also a calling for us.
See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
For the creation waits with eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed.
All creation is waiting for God's children to be revealed. When we live out the life of Christ, even the earth benefits along with us.
Look at a tree, a bird or a flower near you. They all belong to God, and God cares for them. How much more does He care for you.
Reflect: What has God entrusted to me to manage? My time, money, body, family, and this earth.

Prayer: Lord of all, everything is Yours. Make me a faithful steward who takes good care of all You have entrusted to me, so that one day You will say to me, “Well done, good and faithful servant.” In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus reign: the earth is Yahweh's, and everything I have is His too.
Build God's kingdom system: within whatever I am responsible for, govern according to God's heart, so that His will is done on earth.
People matter more than things: we manage creation to bless people, not to possess things.

blocks.h: This week: choose one concrete way to care for creation, such as cutting down on waste or picking up litter, and invite a friend to do it with you.
Congratulations on completing the Earth Hall! From a distance that is just right to an earth entrusted to us, you have seen a God who prepared a home for us and watches over it day and night.
Quiz

quiz.e: Only about 1.2 million of them have been named.

quiz.q: According to Genesis 2:15, why did God put the man in the garden of Eden?
quiz.e: Humans are entrusted stewards.

quiz.q: According to Psalm 24:1, to whom do the earth and its fullness belong?
quiz.e: “The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness…”
